findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: app/models/blocked_email.rb does BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value and neither BlockedEmail nor User downcases/normalizes email before this check. PostgreSQL string equality is case-sensitive, so if an admin blocks bad@spammers.org an attacker can register BAD@spammers.org or Bad@Spammers.org, miss the block list, pass EmailValidator, and create the account. The block feature is therefore defeatable by changing case.

findings.title: Validation has DB write side effect, double-counts every signup
findings.body: lib/validators/email_validator.rb calls BlockedEmail.should_block?(value) from validate_each, and should_block? increments match_count and updates last_match_at with save. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, which validates again, so one signup attempt increments match_count twice and touches last_match_at twice. Any other valid?/invalid paths also mutate stats even when the user is never saved, making match_count/last_match_at unreliable for abuse monitoring.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write on match_count loses updates
findings.body: app/models/blocked_email.rb implements stats as record.match_count += 1; record.last_match_at = ...; record.save. Under two concurrent signup attempts with the same blocked email both threads read the same count, increment locally, and save, so one increment is lost. It also runs full validations/callbacks and touches updated_at for a stats counter. Use an atomic increment such as increment_counter/update_counters/update_all instead.

findings.title: Wrong Ember dependent key means rejected email never shows invalid
findings.body: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js declares emailValidation as .property('accountEmail', 'rejectedEmails.@each') but rejectedEmails is an array of plain strings. @each only observes properties on array members, not array membership, so pushObject in createAccount does not invalidate emailValidation. After the server rejects a blocked email the field keeps showing OK until the user edits the email text, defeating the purpose of the rejectedEmails cache.
